rationale: The store's FIRST target-resolution strategy is an EXACT `qualified_name` match, and its index (`SELECT qualified_name, MIN(id) ... GROUP BY qualified_name`) hands a duplicated qualified name to whichever row sorts first. php published no qualified name for a member, so that index was a NAME index and the first strategy was really 'the alphabetically first declaration of this name anywhere in the project'. Measured on the four-file store gate (validation/m14/fixtures/php/owner-resolution-gate.mts): `$this->persist()` written in GammaStore was stored RESOLVED against AlphaStore::persist, and a read off an unknowable local variable resolved to a real class. Every row below is therefore about IDENTITY, and the fixture declares the same member names under several owners so nothing but the qualified spelling separates them. The `forbidSymbols` rows are the pre-fix state stated as an absence — the mutant that reverts this change deletes the field rather than corrupting it, so the unqualified form is what must not be reachable, not merely what must not be preferred.

expectSymbols.name: helperFn
expectSymbols.note: the deliberate omission: an owner that is a NAMESPACE already has php's own identity in `metadata.fqn`, and a dotted second spelling for one declaration is the aliasing this rule removes

expectSymbolCount.name: persist
expectSymbolCount.note: one declaration per OWNER: the same member name under four class-like owners is four distinct declarations, and a rule that merged them by name would be the same defect this fixture exists for

forbidSymbols.name: helperFn
forbidSymbols.note: a namespace-owned declaration must not acquire a qualified name the store would then match member targets against

forbidRelationships.note: implementing an interface method is NOT an override under this analyzer's rule (same-file base, and `php-overrides.ts` derives none here either, cross-checked 2/2 with 0 MISSING). Stated as an absence so that adopting the other rule is a DECISION that turns this row red, not a silent widening of the label
